### Rule 125 : Icon column alignment

**Any icon column (or icon + short text) must be left-aligned.**

Nerd Font icons have variable width depending on the terminal. Left alignment is the only one that guarantees consistent rendering.

| Content type | Alignment |
|-----------------|------------|
| Icon alone | **Left** |
| Icon + short text | **Left** |
| Alphanumeric text | Left (default) |

#### An icon in the first column **is** a column

When a `datatable`'s first column carries a glyph, it is a column in its own
right — not a prefix stuck onto the neighboring text cell.

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | **empty**. The glyph reads in a glance; a header would be naming something that does not need naming, and `eza` does not put one there either. |
| Width | `datatable.IconColumnWidth` (2): the glyph, plus one cell so it does not touch the text. Two, not one — a Nerd Font glyph renders double-width on some terminals, and a single cell would truncate it there. |
| `Sizing` | `SizingFixed`. Nothing to measure. |
| `Less` / `Search` | **none**. It adds no text anyone could type, so filtering stays on the name columns; and a comparator would cost two more cells to fit its sort arrow. |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the glyph has its own column
{
    Title: "", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: datatable.IconColumnWidth,
    Cell: func(r row) string { return r.icon() },
},
{
    Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16,
    Cell:   func(r row) string { return r.Name },
    Search: func(r row) string { return r.Name },
},

// ❌ WRONG — the glyph stuck into the identifying column
{
    Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
    Cell: func(r row) string { return theme.IconDocker + " " + r.Name },
},
```

**What sticking it in costs**, and this is what settles it: the identifying
column spends its width on something that is not the name, and a
`SizingContent` then measures the glyph along with it — so the table's most
contested column reserves two cells for an icon, at every width.

#### An icon's color goes through a **role**, never through the glyph

Rule 122 applies here as everywhere: `Cell` renders the bare glyph, `Style`
colors it. What Rule 125 adds is **where the color comes from** —
`theme.IconStyle(role)`, and a role declared in `theme/iconcolors.go`.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the view names a meaning, the theme answers with a color
Cell:  func(r row) string { return nodeKindIcon(r.node) },
Style: func(r row) lipgloss.Style { return theme.IconStyle(nodeKindRole(r.node)) },

// ❌ WRONG — the view decides the hue
Style: func(r row) lipgloss.Style {
    return lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorSecondary)
},
```

**A codepoint is not a name.** A table of `U+F0849 → ColorSecondary` cannot
be reviewed: nothing on the line says whether the entry is correct, so an
error there is indistinguishable from a deliberate choice. A role can be
discussed, which is why it is the key.

The five roles are overridable via a theme file (`icon_namespace`,
`icon_repository`, `icon_vis_*`) — unlike syntax colors, which are closed
aliases: an icon is the first thing seen on a row, so it is the part of the
palette a user is most likely to have an opinion about.

**All three icon tables declare a `Style`** — `ws`, `:sec`, and the
explorer — and a fourth that did not declare one would be the application's
only monochrome icon column. A missing role shows: the cell falls back to
`ColorText` (see `IconColor`), so an oversight renders ordinary text rather
than nothing.

**The same object keeps its color from one view to another.** A git repo is
`IconRoleRepository` in `ws`, in `:sec`, and in the explorer — the role is
shared, not duplicated. This is the property for which the key is a meaning
rather than a glyph: the three views do not even show the same glyph for it.

**The granularity is that of the action, not that of the type.** `ws`
colors in three classes — repo, directory, file — which are exactly the
three branches of `availability.go`, and **not** a shade per language the
way `eza` does: `.go` versus `.rs` changes no shortcut on the row, so the
color would say nothing. An icon column is colored by what the row lets you
do.

**The color disappears under the cursor**, like that of any colored column:
the selected row is rendered whole by `styles.Selected` (Rule 122). An icon
column therefore cannot be the *only* carrier of a piece of information —
which is why the explorer's kind stays readable another way (the glyph
outside selection, the position in the tree inside it).

The three tables concerned are `ws`, `containers`, and the `:sec` inventory,
and they declare the same constant. `TestAnIconColumnIsUntitledAndTwoCellsWide`
(`internal/ui/datatable`) scans the sources and rejects a titleless column
that invents its own width. It does not see the other half — a glyph stuck
into a text cell is indistinguishable from a name that starts with a
glyph — which stays a matter for review.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Center)` on an icon column
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Right)` on an icon column
- ❌ A title above a glyph column
- ❌ A local width (`colIconFixed`, `statusColumnWidth`, a literal `2`) instead of `datatable.IconColumnWidth`
- ❌ A glyph prefixed inside a text column's cell
- ❌ An icon color chosen in the view instead of a `theme.IconStyle` role
- ❌ A color table indexed by the glyph rather than by meaning
- ❌ An icon column with no `Style`, while the other three have one
- ❌ A role per file type where the row offers the same actions

### Rule 139 : A `datatable`'s body is never replaced — not by a spinner, not by a message

**A `datatable` stays a table, whatever it contains.** Whether it is
loading its data, empty because nothing has run yet, or empty because a
filter no longer matches anything, the rendered body is always
`m.table.View()` — header included, no rows. `datatable.View()` already
does this on its own: a zero-element table renders its header and fills
the rest with the background (`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`). Nothing
in a view therefore needs to detect this case.

What a body would have said instead — loading, the row count, a verdict —
is **the footer's and header's business**, never the body's:

- loading is a `components.Status{Text: "...", Spinner: true}` in the
  footer (Rule 128);
- the row count, or whatever stands in for it (a verdict, a total), is a
  field of `GetHeaderInfo` (`shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Images", Value: "0"}`) —
  it, not the body, answers "what am I looking at."

**Why.** A body that substitutes itself for the table — with a spinner or
with text — loses its header and its columns for as long as the condition
holds, then regains them: the layout jumps on every refresh, every
`ctrl+r`, every keystroke in the filter. The header and the footer, on the
other hand, have a fixed height (Rule 124): what they display changes
without ever moving the table.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the body is always the table; the footer and header speak
func (m Model) renderImagesView() string {
    return m.imageTable.View()
}

func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if text, ok := m.loadingLabel(); ok {
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: text, Spinner: true}
    }
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.actionLine()}
}

func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(_ string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
    return []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
        {Key: "Images", Value: fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(m.imageTable.Visible())), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
    }
}

// ❌ WRONG — the body replaces itself with a spinner
if m.loading && len(m.images) == 0 {
    return theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Loading images...")
}

// ❌ WRONG — the body replaces itself with a message, empty or filtered
if len(m.imageTable.Visible()) == 0 {
    return theme.DimStyle.Render("No images found")
}
```

The spinner's frame is pushed from the `spinner.TickMsg` handler:
`m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(m.spinner.View())`. Without this call the spinner
stays on frame zero, which reads as a hang.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
`theme.SpinnerMessage` in table views. An operation screen with no table
behind it (a `docker pull` in progress) is an exception **declared in the
test**.

**Declared exception: a welcome screen, not a status message.** The empty
`:sec` inventory (`internal/ui/security/inventory.go`, `renderEmptyInventory`)
replaces the body with a paragraph that explains *where scans come from* —
this is not "0 rows," it is first-use onboarding, with more content than a
header field can carry. The distinction: a message that fits in
`GetHeaderInfo` (a count, a status) goes there; text that explains an
entire application flow stays an explicit exception, like the one already
provided for loading.

### Rule 136 : Filter Bar for Tables

**Every table view must use `components.FilterBar` for search and toggle filters. No ad-hoc filter implementations.**

#### Behaviour

| State | Bar visible | Description |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| No filter | ❌ | Bar is completely hidden |
| Toggle filter active | ✅ | Bar shows dimmed placeholder + active token(s) |
| Search mode (after `/`) | ✅ | Bar shows focused text input + active token(s) |
| Search confirmed (query set) | ✅ | Bar shows dimmed placeholder + query token + toggle tokens |

#### Visual

The filter bar forms a **closed rectangle** that visually connects with the viewport's bottom border:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐   ← viewport top border
│  table rows...                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘   ← viewport bottom border (= rectangle top)
│  / cursor...         [tcp]  ·  [LISTEN] │   ← content line with │ sides
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘   ← rectangle bottom border
```

Both lines use `theme.ColorViewportBorder` for `│`, `└`, `┘`, `─` characters.

#### Placement — Footer, not viewport

The filter bar is rendered in `RenderFooter()`, **not** in the viewport content.

- `GetFooterHeight()` returns `baseFooterHeight + filterBar.ExtraHeight()`
- `RenderFooter()` prepends `filterBar.View()` when `filterBar.IsVisible()`
- Table height formula does **not** subtract `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` — the app router handles that via `GetFooterHeight()`

#### Integration Pattern

```go
// In Model struct
filterBar components.FilterBar  // or components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(tokens)

// In GetFooterHeight()
func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
    return 2 + m.filterBar.ExtraHeight() // base (empty line + info) + filter bar
}

// In RenderFooter()
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    var parts []string
    if m.filterBar.IsVisible() {
        parts = append(parts, m.filterBar.View())
    }
    parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), infoLine)
    return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
}

// In resize() / WindowSizeMsg handler — NO ExtraHeight subtraction
tableHeight := m.height - overhead  // overhead = header row only, NOT filterBar.ExtraHeight()
m.table.SetHeight(tableHeight)

// In Update() / key handler — forward keys when in search mode
if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
    m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
    m.applyFilters()
    return m, cmd
}
// "/" key activates search
case "/":
    return m, m.filterBar.ActivateSearch()

// In InEditMode() — propagate to app router
func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
    return m.filterBar.InEditMode() || /* other edit states */
}

// In View() / renderNormalView() — table only, NO filter bar here
func (m Model) renderNormalView() string {
    return m.table.View()
}

// In applyFilters() — use filterBar.SearchQuery() for text filtering
query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
```

#### Toggle filter tokens (views with dedicated filter keys)

Use `components.NewFilterBarWithTokens()` and update token active state when toggle keys are pressed:

```go
// Init
fb := components.NewFilterBarWithTokens([]components.FilterToken{
    {Label: "tcp"},
    {Label: "udp"},
})

// On key "t"
fb.SetTokenActive("tcp", !fb.IsTokenActive("tcp"))
```

#### Rules

- ✅ Use `components.FilterBar` — never re-implement the filter bar locally
- ✅ The frame itself is `components.BarFrame(width, inner)`: that is what
  `FilterBar.View()` calls, and the only path for whatever shares this slot
  without being a filter — the viewer's go-to-line prompt (§3.53). Two
  implementations of the rectangle would be free to diverge on where the
  corners sit.
- ✅ Only one occupant of the slot at a time, and the height does not depend
  on which one — otherwise the panel resizes under the reader whenever one
  opens on top of the other.
- ✅ `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` must be added to `GetFooterHeight()` return value
- ✅ `filterBar.View()` must be prepended in `RenderFooter()` when `filterBar.IsVisible()`
- ✅ `filterBar.InEditMode()` must propagate via the view's `InEditMode()` method
- ✅ `"/"` key must always call `filterBar.ActivateSearch()`
- ❌ Filter bar must NOT be rendered inside the viewport (`View()` / `renderNormalView()`)
- ❌ `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` must NOT be subtracted from table height (app router handles it)
- ❌ `filterInput textinput.Model` fields in view models (use FilterBar instead)

153	| Testability | pure function in the view, table-driven | same |
154	| Contract cost | additive, 3 fields + 1 method | a presentation rule (5 min, H5) frozen into the public API S-07 consumes |
155	
156	**A**: the package keeps describing what the transcripts say; what counts as
157	"idle" is a display policy that depends on the view's clock and chain.
158	
159	Within the package, two ways to count tool calls: (i) a second map keyed per
160	tool call, folded by position like messages (chosen: same oracle argument,
161	commutative, attribution follows the token rule for a message seen in two
162	files); (ii) hang a set of tool keys on `entry` (rejected: the entry is "last
163	line wins", which is exactly what loses blocks written on separate lines).
164	
165	## Design
166	
167	### Package `internal/agentusage` (additive; the contract says add, do not rename)
168	
169	```go
170	// usage.go
171	type Agent struct {
172	    ... // unchanged fields
173	    ToolCalls     int       // distinct tool_use blocks of the agent's transcript (H1, H2)
174	    FirstActivity time.Time // oldest root timestamp of its transcript, UTC; zero if none
175	    LastActivity  time.Time // newest one, UTC; zero if none
176	}
177	
178	// Duration is LastActivity - FirstActivity, or 0 when either is zero.
179	func (a Agent) Duration() time.Duration
180	```
181	
182	`record.go`:
183	
184	```go
185	type wireLine struct {
186	    Type          json.RawMessage `json:"type"`
187	    Timestamp     json.RawMessage `json:"timestamp"`
188	    APIBlockIndex json.RawMessage `json:"apiBlockIndex"`
189	    Version       json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
190	    Message       *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
191	}
192	type wireMessage struct { ...; Content wireBlocks `json:"content"` }
193	
194	// wireBlocks decodes message.content keeping each block's type and id only.
195	// Anything that is not an array (a user line's string content), and any
196	// malformed element, yields no block and never an error: a bad content array
197	// costs the tool count of that line, never its usage.
198	type wireBlocks []wireBlock
199	func (b *wireBlocks) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error
200	type wireBlock struct { Type, ID string } // input, text, thinking, name: never declared
201	
202	type toolRef struct { id string; abi int; idx int } // abi -1 when absent
203	type record struct {
204	    ... // unchanged
205	    At    time.Time // root timestamp in UTC; zero if absent or not RFC 3339
206	    Tools []toolRef // tool_use blocks of an "assistant" line (H2); nil otherwise
207	}
208	```
209	
210	- `At` is parsed with `time.RFC3339Nano` and **normalised with `.UTC()`**:
211	  the oracle compares `Usage` with `reflect.DeepEqual`, and two equal instants
212	  written `Z` and `+00:00` must have one representation.
213	- `kindIgnored` and `kindSynthetic` records now carry `At` (they used to carry
214	  only `Version`); `kindUnreadable` carries nothing, as today.
215	
216	`table.go`:
217	
218	```go
219	type toolKey struct { msg, block string } // block = "id:"+toolID or "ix:"+abi+"."+idx
220	type toolEntry struct { last pos; agent string } // greatest position wins (absorb)
221	type span struct { first, last time.Time }      // min / max, order-free
222	
223	type table struct {
224	    ... // unchanged
225	    tools     map[toolKey]*toolEntry
226	    toolsNoID map[string]int  // per agent: tool_use blocks of lines without message.id
227	    spans     map[string]span // per agent key
228	}
229	```
230	
231	- `addLine`: after the existing switch, `t.noteTime(agent, r.At)` for every
232	  kind but unreadable, and `t.addTools(agent, p, r)` when `len(r.Tools) > 0`
233	  (already filtered by H2). Inside one line, blocks with the same key count
234	  once.
235	- `mergeSkipping` merges `tools` (absorb by position), adds `toolsNoID`,
236	  merges `spans` (min/max). `mergeCapped`'s no-id spill does not touch tools:
237	  no-id lines are counters already.
238	- `finishWith` sets `ToolCalls` (entries whose `last.agent` matches + the
239	  no-id counter) and `FirstActivity` / `LastActivity` from `spans`, through
240	  the same `idx` map as tokens. Agents absent from the maps keep zeros.
241	- **`hasLines()` also returns true when `len(t.tools) > 0`,
242	  `len(t.toolsNoID) > 0` or `len(t.spans) > 0`.** A tool-result line now
243	  changes `LastActivity`, so it must make the delta non-empty (and advance
244	  `Activity.LastChange`). A line with no timestamp and nothing else (`mode`,
245	  `last-prompt`, today's test lines) stays Empty: the existing Empty tests
246	  keep passing because `msgLine`/`ln` write no timestamp.
247	
248	### View `internal/ui/agentusageview`
249	
250	```go
251	// status.go
252	type runState int
253	const (stateUnknown runState = iota; stateRunning; stateIdle; stateDone)
254	func (s runState) label() string // "unknown", "running", "idle", "done"
255	
256	// statusClock is what the states are computed against: when the last read
257	// finished, and whether the session counts as alive (Q1 A: the chain is live).
258	type statusClock struct { now time.Time; alive bool }
259	
260	// agentStates returns one state per agent, same order (H4, H5).
261	func agentStates(agents []agentusage.Agent, c statusClock) []runState
262	
263	// cmd.go, next to quietPeriod
264	var idleAfter = 5 * time.Minute
265	```
266	
267	Rules of `agentStates` (one table-driven test per line):
268	
269	| Agent | Condition | State |
270	|---|---|---|
271	| sub-agent | `StateFinished` | `done` |
272	| sub-agent | `StateUnfinished` | `running`, or `idle` if quiet > `idleAfter` (alive or not: the meta says unfinished) |
273	| sub-agent | `StateUnknown`, alive | `running` / `idle` as above |
274	| sub-agent | `StateUnknown`, not alive | `unknown` |
275	| orchestrator | alive | `idle` if own quiet > `idleAfter` and no sub-agent is `running`; else `running` |
276	| orchestrator | not alive | `unknown` |
277	
278	"quiet > idleAfter" = `!LastActivity.IsZero() && c.now.Sub(LastActivity) > idleAfter`.
279	
280	```go
281	// agents.go
282	type agentRow struct { ...; state runState }
283	func agentRows(u agentusage.Usage, tree bool, c statusClock) []agentRow // was (u, tree)
284	func formatDuration(d time.Duration, known bool) string
285	
286	// model.go
287	clock statusClock // written in Update only; zero = not alive, so nothing is "running" before a read
288	
289	// selection.go — split so a state refresh does not clear the error footer
290	func (m Model) withRows(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model  // rows, selection, remeasure (today's withUsage body minus the flags)
291	func (m Model) withUsage(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model // withRows + clear agentsLoading/agentsErr (unchanged behaviour)
292	```
293	
294	Columns, inserted after ID (H6, H7):
295	
296	| Title | Sizing | MinWidth | Optional | Cell | Style | Search |
297	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
298	| State | Fixed | 7 | yes | `r.state.label()` | idle → `SeverityTextStyle("MEDIUM")`, unknown → `DimStyle`, else default | the label |
299	| Tools | Fixed | 5 | yes | `formatTokens(int64(r.ToolCalls))` | dim at 0 | — |
300	| Duration | Fixed | 8 | yes | `formatDuration(r.Duration(), !r.FirstActivity.IsZero())` | dim when `-` or `0s` | — |
301	
302	`formatDuration` floors, like `formatTokens`: unknown → `-`; `< 1 min` →
303	`45s`; `< 1 h` → `3m07s`; `< 24 h` → `1h05m`; `< 100 d` → `2d03h`; else `>99d`.
304	At most 6 cells.
305	
306	Expected drop order (Rule 116 budget: width − 2, +2 per rendered column;
307	`threeSubs()` gives Agent 14, Model 12): all columns need 124. 100 cols (98) →
308	drop Cache write, Cache read, In → **Agent, ID, State, Tools, Duration, Model,
309	Out, Total, Share**. 80 cols (78) → also Model → **Agent, ID, State, Tools,
310	Duration, Out, Total, Share** (77). 60 cols (58) → also Duration, Tools,
311	State → **Agent, ID, Out, Total, Share** (unchanged from S-04).
312	
313	### Flow in `handleUsageDelta` (the trap: an idle flag needs no new data)
314	
315	Today an Empty delta changes nothing on screen, so an agent would **never**
316	turn idle: it is idle precisely because nothing arrives. New order, after a
317	successful `Apply` (extract to `applyRead(msg)` to stay under Rule 201's
318	limits):
319	
320	1. `settled := !m.fullPending && m.agg.Activity().Settled(msg.at, quietPeriod)`
321	   — computed **once**, used for both the clock and the stop decision.
322	2. `m.clock = statusClock{now: msg.at, alive: !settled}`.
323	3. `u := m.usage`; if Full or non-Empty, `u = m.agg.Usage()` (no deep copy every
324	   2 s for nothing).
325	4. `m = m.withUsage(u, msg.delta.Full())` **on every successful read**: same
326	   population → no `Remeasure`, selection kept by key.
327	5. Then the existing `fullPending` / stop / next tick logic, unchanged.
328	
329	`failRead` takes the message (it needs `msg.at`): on `os.ErrNotExist`, set
330	`m.clock = statusClock{now: msg.at, alive: false}` and `m = m.withRows(m.usage,
331	false)` — **`withRows`, not `withUsage`**, or the red footer would be cleared.
332	Any other failure leaves the rows and the clock as they are (not an update).
333	`cycleAgentSort` passes `m.clock`. `openSelected` and `closeAgents` reset
334	`m.clock` to zero.

574	
575	- 1 → 2 → {3, 4} in parallel → 5 → 6 → 7.
576	- Step 4 needs only the three `Agent` fields: if the coder lands them first (a
577	  one-commit stub of step 2), step 4 can start right after step 1.
578	
579	## Risks / irreversible
580	
581	- **Public API (irreversible once S-07 consumes it)**: three fields and one
582	  method on `Agent`. Additive only; names chosen so S-07 does not need a rename.
583	- **Privacy surface grows**: `message.content` is now decoded on every line
584	  (block type and id). Mitigations: a reflect test pins `wireBlock` to two
585	  fields; ids never leave the package; the sentinel planted in a tool id. Ask
586	  `security` to review step 1 and step 3.
587	- **Format drift**: `apiBlockIndex` and the one-block-per-line layout are
588	  undocumented. H1's key does not depend on either when `tool_use.id` exists.
589	  If a future client stops writing the root `type`, tool calls fall to 0
590	  silently: the fixture "other version" could pin that later (not in this story).
591	- **Performance**: the content array of every `assistant` line is walked a
592	  second time (block type and id). Lines reach 1.3 MB. The benchmark in step 3
593	  is the guard.
594	- **Durations mislead on resumed sessions**: wall clock from the first to the
595	  last line, days apart if the transcript was resumed. Documented, not fixed.
596	- **Clock skew (S-08)**: idle compares the transcript's own clock with this
597	  machine's; a sandbox with a skewed clock shows wrong idle flags. Documented.
598	- **Q1 A's blind spot**: a session waiting at the prompt reads `unknown` after
599	  5 min. Q1 B fixes it at the cost above.
600	- **Nothing is written to disk, no new dependency.**

1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	Two pieces: the data layer `internal/agentusage` (sections up to
7	"Verification") and the `:agent-usage` view `internal/ui/agentusageview`
8	(last section, DEVDESK-41).
9	
10	## What the package is for
11	
12	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
13	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
14	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
15	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
16	
17	What it does **not** do:
18	
19	- no cost, price or quota computation;
20	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
21	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import (the view lives in `internal/ui/agentusageview`);
22	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
23	
24	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
25	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
26	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`,
27	`ListSessions`, `Session`, `Listing`, and, since DEVDESK-44, `Cursor`, `Delta`,
28	`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `NewAggregate`, `Activity`, `ErrStaleDelta`)
29	is consumed by S-03b, S-04, S-05a and S-05b (DEVDESK-45). Changing a field is a
30	change to those stories; add, do not rename.
31

63	
64	## Transcript format
65	
66	```
67	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
68	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
69	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
70	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
71	```
72	
73	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
74	stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
75	`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
76	Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
77	`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
78	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
79	
80	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
81	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
82	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
83	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
84	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
85	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
86	  (`MetaMissing`);
87	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
88	  sub-agents.
89	
90	## Aggregation rules
91	
92	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
93	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
94	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
95	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
96	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
97	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
98	  increments `NoMessageID`.
99	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
100	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
101	  lines).
102	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
103	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
104	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
105	  decides how to show it.
106	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
107	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
108	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
109	  silently.
110	
111	## Tolerance
112	
113	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
114	
115	- Unknown fields are ignored.
116	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
117	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
118	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
119	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
120	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
121	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
122	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
123	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
124	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
125	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
126	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
127	  `MetaUnreadable`.
128	
129	## Incremental reading (DEVDESK-44)
130	
131	`ParseSession` reads a whole session once. A view that keeps a session open
132	needs to follow it as it grows without reading a multi-MB transcript again on
133	every update. `incremental.go` (reading, `Aggregate`, `Activity`) and `table.go`
134	(the merge) do that. There is no tick, no `gen` and no UI here: wiring them is
135	S-05b (DEVDESK-45).
136	
137	```go
138	agg := agentusage.NewAggregate(parent)       // no I/O
139	d, err := agentusage.ReadDelta(agg.Cursor()) // in a tea.Cmd (Rule 110)
140	err = agg.Apply(d)                           // in Update(); ErrStaleDelta if d is not from agg.Cursor()
141	u := agg.Usage()                             // same shape as ParseSession
142	agg.Cursor().Rewound()                       // ctrl+r: next ReadDelta is Full
143	```
144	
145	### How a file is read
146	
147	Each file of the session has a read position (`fileCursor`): the `offset` just
148	past the last complete line folded in, the `size` seen at the last read, the
149	identity (`os.FileInfo`) of the handle opened, and a few flags below.
150	
151	- **Unchanged file: `Lstat` only.** If the `Lstat` size equals the size seen and
152	  `os.SameFile` matches the identity, the file is not opened. A session that
153	  no longer writes costs one `Lstat` per transcript, one per meta file and one
154	  `ReadDir` of `subagents/`, and no content read. A cursor holding an
155	  `IssueReadError` is never "quiet": the bytes after the failure are read again.
156	- **Append: read from `offset`.** The file is opened (through `openPlain`), the
157	  handle is `Stat`-ed, and the read resumes at `offset`.
158	- **A half-written last line is held back and read again.** `offset` stops at
159	  the end of the last complete line. The next read seeks there and reads the
160	  incomplete line from its start, now hopefully complete. No bytes are kept in
161	  the cursor, so a `Cursor` stays a small copyable value and a `\r\n` or a
162	  UTF-8 sequence split across two reads needs no stitching. The file is listed
163	  in `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles` while the incomplete line lasts. Cost: at most
164	  `MaxLineBytes+2` bytes read again per file per update, only while a line is
165	  half written.
166	- **An oversized line still being written is skipped, not held.** If the
167	  incomplete tail already exceeds `MaxLineBytes+2`, the cursor stores where that
168	  line started (`skipFrom`) and the next read resumes at the end of what was
169	  read (the stored size), skipping up to the next `\n`. The line is counted
170	  **once** in `OversizedLines`, at its start. If the newline never comes, it is
171	  dropped silently, as `ParseSession` does.
172	- **Anything that is not an append restarts the whole session.** The delta is
173	  then `Full()` and every file is read from byte 0, by the same code as
174	  `ParseSession`. Triggers: a file read before is gone, is a link or not
175	  regular, fails to open, has another identity (`os.SameFile` from the open
176	  handle, so a rotation is seen), is smaller than the size seen, or the byte
177	  just before `offset` is not `\n` (a 1-byte `ReadAt` guard against a
178	  truncate-and-regrow). A per-file patch is not possible: a message overwritten
179	  across files cannot be un-counted. A file that appears (a new sub-agent) is
180	  not a trigger: it is read from 0 inside a normal delta. A first read, or a
181	  `Rewound` cursor, is Full too.
182	- **Read errors and open failures are states, not events.** An `IssueReadError`
183	  or `IssueOpenFailed` describes the *last* read of that file and is cleared by
184	  a later successful read, as a fresh `ParseSession` would show. Unreadable and
185	  oversized lines are events: counted once each, since each byte range is
186	  folded once.
187	
188	### Meta files
189	
190	`ReadDelta` never opens a meta file whose `Lstat` size and mtime did not change
191	(and that was already known). It lists them with `Lstat` instead of
192	`openPlain`; `LocateSession` is unchanged and still opens them. A meta file is
193	read again when it appears or when its size or mtime differs.
194	
195	### The incremental result equals `ParseSession`
196	
197	This is the oracle of the whole feature: for the same final files,
198	`Apply`-ing any sequence of deltas gives the `Usage` `ParseSession` gives
199	(the tests compare them with `reflect.DeepEqual`: fixtures fed in chunks, seeded
200	random sessions, a fuzz target). It holds because every line gets a position
201	(`pos{rank, off}`: the file rank in `ParseSession`'s reading order, then the
202	byte offset) and the rules are functions of positions, not of arrival time:
203	
204	- per message key, the line with the **greatest** position wins;
205	- `CrossFileDuplicates` is, over all keys, the number of distinct files minus one;
206	- models, versions and `Diagnostics.Files` follow the **smallest** position,
207	  which is first appearance in a sequential read.
208	
209	The merge is associative and commutative. Sub-agents may therefore be read in
210	any order and appear between two updates.
211	
212	### Declared exceptions to the equality
213	
214	These are deliberate. A test that expects strict equality must avoid them.
215	
216	1. **The 100-issue cap per file keeps the smallest positions.** The cap on
217	   `IssueUnreadable`/`IssueOversized` entries (see "Limits and caps") used to
218	   keep the first 100 *to arrive*. It now keeps the 100 *smallest positions* of
219	   the file, which is what makes it independent of how reads were cut. Only
220	   *which* 100 changes, and only for a file with more than 100; the counters
221	   are unaffected. Accepted by the user (DEVDESK-44).
222	2. **`maxNoIDEntries` is applied in the `Aggregate`.** Past 100000 lines
223	   without a message id, which lines get no table entry (are "spilled": still
224	   counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`) depends on how reads were
225	   cut, not only on position. Totals stay exact; this is the one place the
226	   merge is not commutative. Within a single merge the earliest positions are
227	   kept. The models a spill contributes are also kept by arrival order (up to
228	   the 64-per-agent cap). Not asserted equal by the tests.
229	3. **An unreadable meta file** (for example `chmod 000`) is `MetaUnreadable`
230	   through `ReadDelta` but `MetaMissing` through `ParseSession(LocateSession(…))`,
231	   because `LocateSession` opens the meta file to check it and treats a failure
232	   as absent. Because metas are compared by `Lstat` size and mtime, an
233	   unreadable meta stays unreadable after `chmod +r` until it is rewritten.
234	4. **An unopenable listed file is not a `ReadDelta` error.** `ReadDelta` fails
235	   when the session cannot be listed: the parent is missing, a link, not a
236	   regular file, or the directories cannot be read. If a listed file cannot be
237	   opened (for example `chmod 000`), or is removed between the `Lstat` and the
238	   open, the delta carries an `IssueOpenFailed` on that file: it is `Full()`
239	   the first time, then `Empty()` while the issue persists. The caller can look
240	   at the file's `FileIssue`, in `Usage().Diagnostics.Files`. `ParseSession`
241	   turns the same case on the parent into an error. When `ReadDelta` does
242	   return an error, the caller must not treat the session as settled:
243	   `Activity` keeps its last applied state.
244	
245	### Ownership and stale deltas
246	
247	`Aggregate` has no mutex: the goroutine of `Update()` owns it (Rule 110). A
248	`Cursor` is a deep copy holding no pointer, map or shared slice except the
249	immutable `os.FileInfo`, so `ReadDelta` can run in a `Cmd` while `Update()`
250	goes on. `Apply` takes ownership of the `Delta`; `Usage()` returns a deep copy.
251	
252	A `Cursor` carries the aggregate's identity and a sequence number bumped by every
253	`Apply`. A delta read from anything but the aggregate's current cursor makes
254	`Apply` return `ErrStaleDelta` and change nothing: two reads started from the
255	same cursor cannot both be applied. The caller's own generation counter stays
256	its first filter. **Rule for S-05b: keep a single read in flight per
257	`Aggregate`.**
258	
259	### Activity and `Settled`
260	
261	`Aggregate.Activity()` returns `Activity{LastChange, Unfinished}`.
262	
263	- `LastChange` is the newest mtime among the parent, the sub-agents and the
264	  metas, as of the last applied delta that found a change, capped at the time
265	  of that read (an mtime in the future counts as "now"). It is zero before the
266	  first `Apply`. A delta that is `Empty()` does not advance it, so a bare
267	  `touch` (mtime changes, content does not) does not count as activity.
268	- `Unfinished` counts sub-agents whose readable meta says `finished: false`
269	  (`StateUnfinished`). `StateUnknown` does **not** count: the quiet period covers
270	  them, otherwise a session from a client that writes no `finished` key would
271	  be polled forever.
272	- `LastChange` never moves back: if the newest file disappears, the previous
273	  value is kept.
274	- `Settled(now, quiet)` is true when something was applied, no transcript
275	  (parent or sub-agent) has an `IssueOpenFailed` or `IssueReadError` (the
276	  poller keeps trying while such a failure lasts), no sub-agent is unfinished, and
277	  `now - LastChange >= quiet`. `quiet` is the caller's parameter. A poller
278	  that stops on `Settled` stays stale if the session resumes after more than
279	  `quiet` of idleness, until `ctrl+r` or re-entering the session.
280	
281	### Known limits and risks
282	
283	- **Append-only is assumed, not verified.** A file rewritten **at the same
284	  size**, or rewritten so that the byte before `offset` is still `\n`, is not
285	  detected until the next Full read (`ctrl+r`). A reused inode on ext4 is only
286	  protected by the size comparison and the guard byte.
287	- **Check-then-open window (`safeopen.go`).** Between the `Lstat` in
288	  `readFile` and the `os.Open` in `openPlain`, a file swapped for a FIFO blocks
289	  the call. This already existed (see "Known risk" below); it is now exercised on
290	  every update that sees growth, not once per open. Possible direction:
291	  `O_NONBLOCK` on Unix. Until then, S-05b must keep one read in flight per
292	  `Aggregate`, so a blocked read cannot pile up.
293	- **The message-id table is not bounded.** The table holds one entry per
294	  distinct `message.id` for as long as the `Aggregate` lives. `ParseSession`
295	  had the same property for the duration of one call. Only line length and
296	  lines without id are bounded.
297	- **Very long `MessageID`s are not hashed.** An id of up to a line's length is
298	  kept as the map key.
299	- **Windows is not covered by CI** (Linux only). File identity is taken from
300	  the open handle's `Stat()`, not from `Lstat`, because Go fills the Windows
301	  identity lazily by path and would read the *new* file after a rotation.
302	  Check by hand before a release.
303	
304	## Privacy
305	
306	`ParseSession` returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool
307	input, description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
308	
309	**Amendment (DEVDESK-41): `cwd` is now read and displayed.** `ListSessions`
310	alone reads it, to tell sessions apart by project. It is the first non-empty
311	string `cwd` found in the first 8 MiB of a transcript (twice `MaxLineBytes`, so
312	one maximal line can be skipped); the scan stops there and nothing else of the
313	transcript is kept. The view shows the **full path**, with the home folder
314	folded to `~`. The path is sanitized and capped, and is **never logged**: the
315	view logs a failed listing, but its error carries a base name only. A `Usage`
316	still carries no path. This replaces the earlier wording that no path was ever
317	read.
318	
319	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
320	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
321	- Text that comes from disk goes through `sanitize`: labels (model, version,
322	  agent type, session and agent IDs, file names; `sanitizeLabel`, cut to 128
323	  bytes) and the `cwd` (cut to 4096 bytes). Replaced by `?`: invalid UTF-8
324	  bytes, every control character (C0, DEL and **C1**, so a raw or encoded
325	  0x9B CSI is caught) and every format character (Unicode category **Cf**:
326	  bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks). Text read from disk reaches a
327	  terminal, where an escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override
328	  would reorder what follows.
329	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
330	- `Cursor`, `Delta` and `Aggregate` hold full paths in unexported fields. They
331	  are never logged: `String`/`GoString` (and so `%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`) print counts
332	  only. Errors from `ReadDelta` name base names. A `Usage` still holds no path.
333	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
334	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
335	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
336	  an error.
337	
338	## Limits and caps
339	
340	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
341	
342	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
343	|---|---|---|
344	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
345	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. The 100 kept are the **smallest positions** of the file, not the first to arrive (declared exception, see "Incremental reading"). `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
346	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together), enforced in the `Aggregate` | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry. Which lines spill can depend on how reads were cut (declared exception) |
347	| Bytes read per update (`ReadDelta`) | the appended bytes, plus at most `MaxLineBytes+2` per file with a half-written line, plus 1 guard byte per file read | a Full delta costs what `ParseSession` costs |
348	| Message-id entries | **not bounded** | one entry per distinct `message.id`, held as long as the `Aggregate` lives |
349	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
350	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
351	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
352	| Sessions listed (`ListSessions`) | 10000 | the oldest are dropped and counted in `Listing.Omitted` |
353	| `cwd` probe (`ListSessions`) | first 8 MiB of each kept transcript | `Project` is `""` |
354	| `Session.Project` length | 4096 bytes | truncated |
355	
356	The 10000 cap applies after the directories are read: there is **no bound on
357	memory or time before it**. Every entry of every project directory is read and
358	stat-ed first, so a very large projects tree costs that much before the cap
359	trims the result. Only the `cwd` probe, run on the kept sessions, is bounded.
360	
361	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
362	
363	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
364	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
365	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
366	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
367	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
368	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
369	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
370	documented in the code. `ListSessions` has the same exposure: it opens each
371	kept transcript through `openPlain` to read its `cwd`, so a FIFO swapped in
372	there can block the listing (and so the view's read, which runs in a `Cmd`).
373	Carried over unchanged, not closed. `ReadDelta` opens transcripts through the
374	same `openPlain`, so it has the same exposure, now repeated on every update that
375	sees growth (see "Known limits and risks" under "Incremental reading").
376	
377	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
378	
379	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
380	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
381	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
382	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
383	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.
384	
385	## Verification
386	
387	- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
388	  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
389	- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
390	  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
391	  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
392	  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
393	  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
394	- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
395	  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
396	  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
397	  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
398	  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
399	  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
400	  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
401	  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:
402	
403	  ```bash
404	  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
405	  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
406	  ```
407	
408	  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
409	  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
410	  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
411	  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
412	  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
413	  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
414	  sessions and must never be committed.
415	
416	  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
417	  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
418	  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
419	  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.
420	
421	## The `:agent-usage` view
422	
423	`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
424	Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
425	and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or
426	`enter` opens the selected session's agents (DEVDESK-42, below).
427	
428	| Column | Content |
429	|---|---|
430	| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
431	| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
432	| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |
433	
434	- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
435	  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
436	- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
437	  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
438	- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
439	  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
440	  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
441	  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
442	  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
443	- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
444	  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
445	  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
446	- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
447	  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
448	  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
449	  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
450	  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
451	  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
452	  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
453	  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
454	  are dated, not wrong.
455	- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
456	  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
457	  the model.
458	
459	### Second level: the session's agents (DEVDESK-42)
460	
461	`→`/`enter` on a session opens its agents; `←`/`esc` goes back to the list.
462	`agents.go` builds the table, `availability.go` decides what the keys allow.
463	
464	| Column | Content |
465	|---|---|
466	| Agent | `orchestrator`, then each sub-agent's type behind `├─ ` / `└─ ` in tree order, bare when sorted (`unknown` when the meta file gave none). `/` matches the role only. |
467	| ID | the sub-agent's short ID (`shortAgentIDs`): the smallest common length >= 8 runes at which all IDs of the session differ, capped at each ID's own length. `-` for the orchestrator, `?` for a sub-agent with an empty ID. `/` matches the full ID here. Never dropped, so two agents of one type stay apart. |
468	| Model | the models the agent used, comma-separated; `-` (dim) when none. `Optional`. |
469	| In, Out, Cache read, Cache write, Total | token counts. On a narrow terminal the drop order is `Cache write`, `Cache read`, `In`, `Model`. `Out` and `Total` stay. |
470	| Share | the agent's part of the session total (`Usage.Total().Total()`), see below. Fixed width. |
471	
472	- **Share (`share.go`).** Tenths of a percent, floored, computed on 128 bits
473	  (`bits.Mul64`/`Div64`) so no product overflows; a part is clamped to
474	  `[0, total]`. The orchestrator absorbs the rounding residue, so the column
475	  sums to `100.0%`; the residue is clamped at 0 when saturated totals overshoot.
476	  With no orchestrator row nothing is absorbed. A session with no tokens gives
477	  `noShare` and the cell shows a dim `-`. Rendered as `12.3%`.
478	- **Sort.** Only `Total` is sortable (`Less`, `DescFirst`). `.` cycles tree,
479	  `Total ▼`, `Total ▲`, tree. A table that opened unsorted returns to the tree
480	  after the last step. `agentRows(usage, tree)` draws the branches only when no
481	  sort is active: a sorted list is flat, and a branch there would lie about who
482	  is whose child. `cycleAgentSort` rebuilds the rows after each press and
483	  remeasures the Agent column. The sort lives in the table, so it survives
484	  opening another session and `ctrl+r`.
485	
486	- **Compact tokens.** `formatTokens` floors to one decimal (`1099` is `1.0k`,
487	  never `1.1k`) and drops the decimal from 100 of a unit up. Units: `k M B T`.
488	  Zeros are dim (Rule 122).
489	- **`≥` on Out.** A sub-agent whose output is partial (`Agent.PartialOutput()`,
490	  transcript still being written) shows `≥ ` before its Out count: a floor, not
491	  an exact value. The orchestrator never does.
492	- **Flat tree, two levels.** Whatever `SpawnDepth` a sub-agent has, it is a
493	  direct child of the orchestrator in the table. Order: orchestrator first, then
494	  sub-agents sorted by ID (stable) until the user sorts by Total.
495	- **Breadcrumb.** `Sessions › <project> › <short ID>` sits in the footer, one row
496	  above the filter bar and the message line (Rule 123), and adds one row to
497	  `GetFooterHeight`.
498	- **Header**: `Agents`, `Tokens` (sum of Total), both following the filter, and
499	  `Updates` (`live` or `paused`, see "Live updates").
500	- **Footer status**: a failed read (red, "Failed to read this session — check
501	  logs"), then loading (a full read only; spinner, "Reading session..."), then, when
502	  `Diagnostics.Degraded()`, a warning "Totals are approximate — some transcript
503	  data could not be read".
504	- **Availability (Rule 130).** The shortcut keys are identical at both levels;
505	  only `Disabled` changes, computed once in `availability()` and read by
506	  `GetShortcuts` and by the handlers through `guard`, which refuses with a Warn
507	  carrying the reason. `→` is greyed with no session selected or already inside
508	  a session; `esc` at the session list. `.` is always available, at both levels, and shown as `. Sort` in the header.
509	- **Rule 110.** `readDeltaCmd` calls `ReadDelta` inside a `Cmd` on a copy of the
510	  `Cursor` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches the model and the
511	  `Aggregate`. Each read carries `agentGen`, bumped on open, on a full `ctrl+r`,
512	  on leaving the level (`closeAgents`), on `Leave` and on resume; an answer with
513	  another generation, or arriving after the user went back, is dropped.
514	  `ctrl+r` at the agents level reads the open session again from the start.
515	
516	#### Live updates (DEVDESK-45)
517	
518	The agents level follows a session that is still being written. It uses the
519	incremental API of DEVDESK-44 (`Cursor`, `Delta`, `Aggregate`), not
520	`ParseSession`: the model holds one `*Aggregate` per open session, and each
521	read applies a `Delta` to it.
522	
523	**The polling chain.** Opening a session starts a full read (cursor
524	`Rewound()`, spinner, "Reading session..."). Each answer schedules the next
525	step: wait `pollInterval` (2 s, `pollTickCmd`), then `startRead(false)` reads
526	from the cursor, silently (no spinner). At most one read and one tick exist per
527	`agentGen`: `reading` blocks a tick that arrives while a read is in flight, and
528	a tick or an answer of another generation is dropped. An empty delta changes
529	nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
530	If `Aggregate.Apply` rejects a delta (not read from the current cursor), the
531	view logs it and reads again from the aggregate's own cursor.
532	
533	**When the chain stops.** After a successful read, the chain ends if
534	`Activity().Settled(at, quietPeriod)` is true: `quietPeriod` is 5 min, and a
535	session with any sub-agent not finished is never settled (see "Activity and
536	`Settled`"). It also ends on `os.ErrNotExist` (the parent transcript was
537	deleted). Any other error retries after another 2 s from the same cursor and
538	keeps the rows already shown; the footer says "Failed to read this session —
539	check logs", and only the first failure of a streak is logged. A successful
540	read clears the error.
541	
542	**`pollStopped`.** The model records the end of the chain as `pollStopped`
543	(true = stopped). The plan spoke of a `live` field; the code has the opposite
544	sense, so that the zero value of a fresh model is "polling". It makes a late
545	tick of the same generation start nothing, and every full read clears it.
546	
547	**The `Updates` header.** `Updates › live` while an aggregate is open and
548	`pollStopped` is false, `paused` otherwise. It is derived on every frame
549	(`updatesState`), not stored. Pressing `ctrl+r` on a settled session clears
550	`pollStopped` for the duration of the full read, so the header can go
551	`paused → live → paused` in a few frames when the session is still quiet.
552	
553	**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
554	everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
555	never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
556	starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.
557	
558	**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
559	- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
560	  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
561	  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
562	  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
563	- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
564	  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
565	  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
566	  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
567	  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
568	  has its spinner.
569	
570	**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
571	stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`
572	counting the earlier agents with the same ID (two twins with one ID keep their
573	own keys). Keys are computed on the canonical order (`agentRows`), never on the
574	sorted or filtered one, otherwise twins would swap keys whenever they swap
575	ranks. `withUsage` records the key under the cursor before rebuilding the rows
576	and puts the cursor back on it, whatever the filter and the sort did to the
577	order; if the agent is gone, the cursor is clamped.
578	
579	**Column widths are not reshuffled every two seconds.** `withUsage` calls
580	`Remeasure()` only after a full read, or when the *population* changed. The
581	population is the list of keys plus the models of each row (`populationOf`):
582	counts change on every delta and do not count. An agent's type can arrive late
583	(its meta file is written after its transcript); the type is deliberately not
584	part of the population, so a late type stays truncated to the width measured
585	earlier until the next `ctrl+r` or change of population.
586	
587	**The sessions list is not live.** Only the open session is polled. The list
588	of sessions is read on entry and by `ctrl+r` at the sessions level.
589	
590	**Privacy.** `usageDeltaMsg` implements `String` and `GoString` so that `%v`
591	and `%+v`, `%#v` print only `gen`, the delta's own redacted form and whether
592	the read failed. A `Delta` holds file paths behind unexported fields, which
593	`fmt` cannot hand to the `Delta`'s redacting methods when the message is
594	dumped. Read errors are logged and never shown.
595	
596	**Known limits, deliberate.**
597	1. *An unreadable parent shows an empty orchestrator.* If the parent
598	   transcript exists but cannot be read (for instance `chmod 000`),
599	   `ReadDelta` returns `err == nil`: the screen shows an orchestrator at 0 and
600	   the warning "Totals are approximate…", where the earlier `ParseSession`
601	   path showed the red "Failed to read this session" footer. Accepted by the
602	   product owner; it is documented here rather than worked around.
603	2. *A session that resumes after `Settled` stays `paused`.* Once the chain has
604	   stopped on a quiet session, nothing polls the file any more. The header
605	   keeps saying `paused` until `ctrl+r` or until the user leaves the view and
606	   comes back (the resume reads the cursor and restarts the chain).
607	3. *A failed `ctrl+r` full read is not replayed.* If the full read started by
608	   `ctrl+r` fails for a cause other than `ErrNotExist`, the retry starts from
609	   the aggregate's cursor and does not rewind it: the `ctrl+r` is lost, and
610	   only the red footer says that something failed. Press `ctrl+r` again.
611	4. *Some exits do not call `Leave`.* The paths that leave the view by another
612	   means than `switchView` (the viewer, netdiag, the path picker) are not
613	   reachable from `:agent-usage` today. If one is added, it has to stop the
614	   chain the way `Leave` does, or a poll would continue under another view.
615	
616	**Privacy.** The view displays the project directory, the date, the session ID,
617	agent types, models and token counts. It never displays or logs the paths of
618	files a session touched, nor any content (prompt, reply, tool input or output):
619	`Usage` holds numbers and labels only, as stated in "Privacy" above.
620	
621	Known limits: the FIFO risk and the lack of a memory or time bound before the
622	10000-session cap (see "Limits and caps") both apply to this view's read. Claude
623	Code deletes old transcripts itself (30 days by default), so older sessions
624	disappear from the list.
625

1	# Test fixtures
2	
3	Every file here is **synthetic**: the shape (keys, nesting, file layout) follows
4	what Claude Code 2.1.302 writes under `~/.claude/projects/`, but every value is
5	invented. No real prompt, answer, path, description or token count was copied.
6	`SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` sits in the `content`, `description`, `cwd` and tool
7	`input` fields of the transcripts, and in the `description` of the `.meta.json`
8	files, on purpose: a test checks that it never reaches a `Usage` value or an
9	error. That check guards `ParseSession`/`Usage` only: since DEVDESK-41 `ListSessions`
10	does read `cwd` on purpose, and its tests (`sessions_test.go`) build their own
11	trees in a temp directory instead of using these fixtures.
12	
13	Layout: `<fixture>/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl`, sub-agents in
14	`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with `agent-<id>.meta.json` beside them.
15	
16	| Fixture | Purpose |
17	|---|---|
18	| `v2.1.302-basic/` | orchestrator + 3 sub-agents, streaming repeats, null/absent usage fields, a `<synthetic>` message, a partial last message, and a `tool-results/` folder that must not be read |
19	| `synthetic-other-version/` | an invented "9.0.0": renamed or absent `usage`, unknown line type, `meta.json` without `finished` |
20	| `damaged/` | a non-JSON line in the middle of a file and a sub-agent file cut mid-JSON without a final newline |
21	
22	Expected totals are written by hand in `parse_test.go`, not computed from these files.
23

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## plane-devops

## Epics

There are no epic tools — an epic is a work item whose type is named "Epic". Work
items always belong to a project; ask which if one is not named.
1. type = `workitem_type resolve` with project_id and name="Epic" — type.id is the type_id.
2. Create: `workitem create` with project_id, type_id=type.id, name=...
3. List: `workitem list` with project_id and pql='type = "<type id>"'.
4. Read / update / delete / nest: `workitem retrieve` / `workitem update` /
   `workitem delete` by work item id (set parent=<work item id> to nest).
5. List an epic's children: `workitem list` with pql='childOf("<EPIC-IDENTIFIER>")'
   using the epic's human-readable identifier (e.g. "PROJ-12") from `workitem retrieve`.

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)
